- Overestimate prices in the early part of the 30-day horizon, especially after sentiment spikes (positive sentiment > 0.5), and correct downward bias in the middle-to-late period.
- Underestimate sharp downward moves after recent price spikes; model tends to overreact to sentiment peaks and fails to capture immediate reversal.
- When sentiment turns negative (e.g., < 0.3), model often overcorrects or underreacts — reduce forecast magnitude by 5–10% in such periods.
- Mean reversion bias: model holds too much upward momentum after recent highs; apply a 3–5 day decay factor to momentum-based components.
- Overshoot after sentiment-driven spikes: if sentiment > 0.7 and price rises > 2% from prior day, reduce forecast by 1–2% for next 3 days.
- Horizon-specific: last 5–7 days of forecast often overestimate true price; apply a 0.8–0.9 multiplier to recent forecast values to align with observed decay.
